summary: Steel fire lookout on Bradden Knob, Fall Creek Falls State Park, TN; built c. 1895 per NRHP (NHLR says 1865); moved 1941 or 1943; NRHP-listed 2015.

facts.design: Eighty-foot skeletal steel tower with bolted connections, four angle-section legs on concrete footers, square cab with a ribbon of windows

access.note: The 2023 park plan says the tower must be made safe before guests can visit. The plan also says access to the tower itself is discouraged. No current opening or closure notice was found. Confirm with Tennessee State Parks before any visit.

visit.trail_note: On Bradden Knob inside Fall Creek Falls State Park; the plan calls for structural work before guests visit

events.note: NRHP: originally constructed ca. 1895, first used as a tourist tower at the Chickamauga Battlefield. NHLR gives 1865 instead.
Moved to present site on Bradden Knob by the CCC per NRHP; Forest Lookouts also says 1941. NHLR says 1943.
Listed July 21, 2015, NRIS 15000444, Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers MPS
May 2023 park facility inventory rates the tower Fair; a resource condition table in the same plan rates it Poor
Lookout house at the foot of the tower (not the tower itself), built around 1950 per park plan

corrections.why: The NRHP nomination gives 2,026 feet (about 617.6 m) for the tower site. The current 522.1 m matches NHLR's 1,713 ft figure, which NHLR attaches to its own coordinates. Editor to confirm which point the record means.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1865 and ties the tower to the battlefield dedication. The NRHP nomination gives ca. 1895, and the Forest Lookouts page gives around 1895. The story uses ca. 1895 and reports NHLR's date as a disagreement.
NHLR says the tower was moved in 1943. The NRHP nomination and Forest Lookouts say 1941. The story uses 1941 and notes the 1943 date.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on construction (NHLR 1865 vs NRHP and Forest Lookouts c. 1895) and the move (NHLR 1943 vs NRHP and Forest Lookouts 1941). The Forest Lookouts 1941 entry describes an existing observation tower converted to a fire detection facility, while the NRHP says the building was moved; both are cited. Condition is inconsistent inside the 2023 park plan: the facility inventory rates the tower Fair, while a resource condition table rates it Poor and says the structure is extremely damaged. NRHP (2015) said overall good. Location: the record uses tnlandforms coordinates (35.6696, -85.3059); NHLR gives 35.657250, -85.347900. Not resolved; please check against the NRHP nomination's own coordinates. No staffing, fire history or current access notice appears in the sources read. A travel listing that says the tower is closed was seen only in search results and not read, so it is not cited. A Grundy County Herald article was seen only in search results and not read.
